rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jews in Medina envied the Prophet and urged him to move to Syria, promising belief; as he set out, the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حسدت اليهود مقام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة فقالوا: إن الأنبياء إنما بعثوا

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن غنم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm says the verse was revealed at Tabuk after the surah had ended, when the Prophet intended Syria and was ordered to return.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن غنم: غزا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم غزوة تبوك لا يريد إلا

rows.speaker: مجاهِد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada relate the threat to Meccans plotting to expel the Prophet; had they expelled him, they would have been swiftly destroyed. Qurtubi says this is sounder because the surah is Meccan and the context mentions Meccans, not Jews.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: نزلت في هم أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The land” means Mecca; Qurtubi supports this by comparing Joseph's reference to Egypt and the town that expelled the Prophet, which is Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { من الأرض } يريد أرض مكة. كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the plotters as all unbelievers conspiring to dislodge the Prophet from Arabia; God prevented them, and their quick disappearance explains the threat.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم الكفار كلهم أن يستخفوه من أرض العرب بتظاهرهم عليه فمنعه

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: Ataa ibn Abi Rabah reads “they would not remain” with a doubled bāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عطاء بن أبي رباح «لا يلبثون» الباء مشددة.

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو بكر وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers have khalafaka, understood as “after you.”
rows.anchor: «خلفك» نافع وابن كثير وأبو بكر وأبو عمرو، ومعناه بعدك.

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحفص وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers have khilafaka; Abu Hatim prefers it by comparison with 9:81, and it too means “after you.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحفص وحمزة والكسائي «خلافك» واختاره أبو حاتم، اعتبارا بقوله:

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic line uses khilafihim in the sense “after them,” illustrating the reading.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
عفت الديار خلافهم فكأنما
بسط الشواطب بينهن حصيرا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari distinguishes khalafaka, “after you,” from khilafaka, “opposing you.”
rows.anchor: «وخلافك» بمعنى مخالفتك ذكره ابن الأنباري.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Except a little” may mean the time from the Quraysh's expulsion of the Prophet until their killing at Badr.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن المدة التي لبثوها بعده ما بين إخراجهم له إلى قتلهم يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it spans the time until the killing of Banu Qurayza and the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir, on the view that the threat concerns Jews.
rows.anchor: الثاني: ما بين ذلك وقتل بني قريظة وجلاء بني النضير

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra parses “the way” as an accusative governed by an implicit “they are punished,” with the verb acting after the preposition is omitted.
rows.anchor: أي يعذبون كسنة من قد أرسلنا فهو نصب بإضمار يعذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes it an accusative under an implied “We established a way.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: انتصب على معنى سننا سنة من قد أرسلنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing supplies an omitted kāf: they will not remain long after you, like the established pattern for earlier messengers; this changes where one pauses in recitation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو منصوب على تقدير حذف الكاف التقدير لا يلبثون خلفك إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established pattern does not fail: His promise is not broken.
rows.anchor: ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا } أي لا خلف في وعدها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the polytheists' schemes, God commands the Prophet to be patient and preserve prayer; prayer also seeks victory over enemies, as in 15:97.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر مكايد المشركين أمر نبيه عليه السلام بالصبر والمحافظة على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes unanimously take this verse to refer to the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية بإجماع من المفسرين إشارة إلى الصلوات المفروضة.

rows.speaker: عمر وابنه وأبو هريرة وابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation defines the sun's duluk as its decline from the middle of the sky.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه زوال الشمس عن كبد السماء قاله عمر وابنه وأبو هريرة وابن عباس

rows.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A second interpretation defines duluk as sunset; it is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: الثاني أن الدلوك هو الغروب قاله علي وابن مسعود وأبي بن

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi explains the two senses by rubbing one's eyes either from the sun's intense glare or to see it at sunset.
rows.anchor: من جعل الدلوك اسما لغروبها فلأن الإنسان يدلك عينيه براحته

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd takes duluk as sunset and cites the expression “the sun set.”
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: دلوكها غروبها. ودلكت براح يعني الشمس أي غابت.

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub's verse uses birāḥ for the sun; the word is read with fatḥa as a sun-name or, in al-Farra's reading, with kasra as a plural meaning palms.
rows.anchor:
وأنشد قطرب:
هذا مقام قدمي رباح

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj's line uses rāḥ for the hand or palm that shields the eyes while pushing the sun away; Ibn al-Aʿrabi explains zahlafa as sliding on a smooth slope.
rows.anchor:
ومنه قول العجاج:
والشمس قد كادت تكون دنفا
أدفعها بالراح كي تزحلفا

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses dālikāt for the setting stars or suns, supporting the sunset sense.
rows.anchor:
قال ذو الرمة:
مصابيح ليست باللواتي تقودها
نجوم ولا بالآفلات الدوالك

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says duluk linguistically means inclination: its beginning is noon decline and its end sunset, so the interval includes Zuhr and Asr and may include Maghrib.
rows.anchor: الدلوك هو الميل في اللغة فأول الدلوك هو الزوال وآخره هو الغروب.

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Some hold that Zuhr's time extends from decline to sunset because the command is tied to duluk, the whole period of inclination; Malik and al-Shafiʿi indicate this in necessity.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب قوم إلى أن صلاة الظهر يتمادى وقتها من الزوال إلى الغروب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Malik, says duluk is the sun's inclination and ghassaq is night gathering into darkness.
rows.anchor: الثانية: قوله تعالى: { إلى غسق الليل } روى مالك عن ابن عباس قال: دلوك الشمس ميلها، وغسق الليل اجتماع الليل وظلمته.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd defines ghassaq as the blackness of night, supported by Ibn Qays's poetic line.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الغسق سواد الليل. قال ابن قيس الرقيات:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations make ghassaq the disappearance of twilight or the arrival of darkness; Zuhayr's verse uses the term at nightfall.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: غسق الليل مغيب الشفق. وقيل: إقبال ظلمته. قال زهير:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word derives from flowing, as in an eye or wound discharging fluid; forms with and without the initial hamza are both used for nightfall.
rows.anchor: وأصل الكلمة من السيلان يقال: غسقت العين إذا سالت، تغسق.

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: On a cloudy day al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym told his muezzin to delay Maghrib until night darkened.
rows.anchor: وكان الربيع بن خثيم يقول لمؤذنه في يوم غيم: أغسق أغسق.

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي والثوري
rows.claim: One view gives Maghrib a single time at sunset, based on Gabriel praying it at the same time on both days; this is the apparent Maliki position among its adherents and a well-known Shafiʿi view.
rows.anchor: فقيل: وقتها وقت واحد لا وقت لها إلا حين تحجب

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه والحسن بن حي وإسحاق وأبو ثور وداود
rows.claim: Another view keeps Maghrib time open until twilight disappears, treating sunset-to-twilight as the full interval of ghassaq.
rows.anchor: فإذا غاب الشفق فقد خرجت من وقت المغرب ودخل وقت العشاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those favoring the longer time cite Abu Musa's report that the Prophet delayed the second day's Maghrib until twilight fell, and argue this later Medinan report supersedes Gabriel's Meccan prayer.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى بالسائل المغرب في اليوم الثاني فأخر حتى كان عند سقوط الشفق

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the longer-time ruling is the famous Maliki position, stated in the Muwattaʾ that Malik taught throughout his life.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن العربي أن هذا القول هو المشهور من مذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi favors the expanded permissible time. The reports can be reconciled: Gabriel shows the preferred prompt time at sunset, while other reports show permissibility until twilight; reconciliation preserves both proofs better than abrogation or preference.
rows.anchor: قلت: القول بالتوسعة أرجح. وقد خرج الإمام الحافظ أبو محمد عبد الغني بن سعيد

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet left Mecca near sunset and did not pray Maghrib until reaching Sarf, nine miles away.
rows.anchor: عن جابر قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من مكة قريبا من غروب الشمس فلم يصل المغرب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra parses Qurʾān as coordinated with prayer: establish the dawn Qurʾān, meaning the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون معطوفا على الصلاة المعنى: وأقم قرآن الفجر أي صلاة الصبح قاله الفراء.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Qurʾān is accusative as an exhortation: attend to the dawn recitation.
rows.anchor: انتصب على الإغراء أي فعليك بقرآن الفجر قاله الزجاج.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The dawn prayer is singled out as Qurʾān because it is the greatest prayer, with long, audible recitation.
rows.anchor: لأن القرآن هو أعظمها، إذ قراءتها طويلة مجهور بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan practice favored a substantial dawn recitation that did not burden the congregation, then long recitation at Zuhr and Friday, light recitation at Maghrib, and moderate recitation at Asr and Isha; some also lighten Asr.
rows.anchor: وقد استقر عمل المدينة على استحباب إطالة القراءة في الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports of unusually short or long recitations in prayers with an established practice are set aside in favor of communal practice; the Prophet rebuked Muʿadh for beginning Isha with al-Baqara and ordered imams to keep prayer easy for people with varied needs.
rows.anchor: فافتتح سورة البقرة. خرجه الصحيح. وبأمره الأئمة بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the dawn prayer Qurʾān supports the principle that prayer requires recitation.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن لا صلاة إلا بقراءة لأنه سمى الصلاة قرآنا.

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The majority require al-Fatiha from imam and solo worshipper in every rakʿa; Malik's well-known position agrees.
rows.anchor: فذهب جمهورهم إلى وجوب قراءة أم القرآن للإمام والفذ في كل ركعة.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik is also reported to require al-Fatiha in most of the prayer, a view held by Ishaq; in another report it is required in one rakʿa, according to al-Mughira and Sahnun.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا أنها واجبة في جل الصلاة. وهو قول إسحاق.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Other reports from Malik say recitation is not obligatory in any part, or only in half the prayer, the latter also attributed to al-Awzaʿi.
rows.anchor: وعنه أن القراءة لا تجب في شيء من الصلاة. وهو أشد الروايات عنه.

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي وأيوب والشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Awzaʿi and Ayyub, and one Shafiʿi view, require recitation from imam, solo worshipper, and follower in every prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن الأوزاعي أيضا وأيوب أنها تجب على الإمام والفذ والمأموم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says the night and day angels witness dawn prayer; Tirmidhi grades this report hasan sahih, and another route includes Abu Saʿid.
rows.anchor: السادسة: قوله تعالى: { كان مشهودا } روى الترمذي عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Bukhari report says congregational prayer has twenty-five times the merit of individual prayer and night and day angels meet at dawn; Abu Hurayra cites this verse.
rows.anchor: فضل صلاة الجميع على صلاة الواحد خمس وعشرون درجة وتجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn prayer is performed early so both angel groups witness it; delay means only one group witnesses it. Malik and al-Shafiʿi therefore prefer praying in the pre-dawn darkness.
rows.anchor: ولهذا المعنى يبكر بهذه الصلاة، فمن لم يبكر لم تشهد صلاته إلا إحدى الفئتين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa prefers combining pre-dawn darkness with later brightness, and, if that is missed, prefers brightness; Qurtubi objects that this opposes the Prophet's consistent early prayer and loses the night angels' witness.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: الأفضل الجمع بين التغليس والإسفار، فإن فاته ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' witnessing does not make dawn prayer neither night nor day: Asr also has both angel groups meeting, yet Asr is daytime by fasting and oath rulings, so dawn too belongs to daytime.
rows.anchor: وهذا مخالف لما كان عليه السلام يفعله من المداومة على

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that night and day angels alternate in attendance and meet at both Asr and Fajr.
rows.anchor: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار فيجتمعون في صلاة العصر وصلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive; the fa connects to an implied command to rise, and “by it” means by the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: «من» للتبعيض. والفاء في قوله «فتهجد» ناسقة على مضمر، أي قم فتهجد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahajjud comes from a word that can mean either sleep or wakefulness; it is alertness after sleep, hence the name for night prayer.
rows.anchor: والتهجد التيقظ بعد رقدة، فصار اسما للصلاة لأنه ينتبه لها.

rows.speaker: الأسود وعلقمة وعبد الرحمن بن الأسود
rows.claim: Al-Aswad, ʿAlqama, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad explain tahajjud as rising from sleep to pray.
rows.anchor: قال معناه الأسود وعلقمة وعبد الرحمن بن الأسود وغيرهم.

rows.speaker: الحجاج بن عمرو
rows.claim: The Companion Hajjaj ibn Amr says a person has not performed tahajjud merely by praying all night: tahajjud is prayer after sleeping, as the Prophet used to do.
rows.anchor: أنه قال: أيحسب أحدكم إذا قام من الليل كله أنه قد تهجد! إنما التهجد الصلاة بعد رقدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, tahajjud names staying awake by casting off sleep, like other words formed for discarding a state; the verse means spending part of the night in prayer and recitation.
rows.anchor: والمعنى في الآية: ووقتا من الليل أسهرته في صلاة وقراءة.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses “as an additional devotion for you” as a special honor for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الثانية: قوله تعالى: { نافلة لك } أي كرامة لك قاله مقاتل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that night prayer was an extra obligation uniquely on the Prophet is unlikely: it treats a duty as a voluntary offering and conflicts with the explicit five-prayer reports.
rows.anchor: قلت: وفي هذا التأويل بعد لوجهين: أحدهما: تسمية الفرض بالنفل، وذلك مجاز لا حقيقة.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A different view, attributed to Aisha, says night prayer was first obligatory on everyone and later abrogated, becoming a voluntary act after the required prayers.
rows.anchor: ثم نسخ الوجوب فصار قيام الليل تطوعا بعد فريضة، كما قالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the abrogation view the command is recommended and addressed to the Prophet, who is forgiven; his voluntary worship raises his rank, while other believers' voluntary worship repairs defects in obligatory acts, as Mujahid and others explain.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون الأمر بالتنفل على جهة الندب ويكون الخطاب للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafila is also explained as a gift, since no gift of happiness is better than being enabled to worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عطية لأن العبد لا ينال من السعادة عطاء أفضل من التوفيق في العبادة.

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: The soundest interpretation of the praised station is the Prophet's intercession for people on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: الأول: وهو أصحها الشفاعة للناس يوم القيامة قاله حذيفة بن اليمان.

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that humanity gathers in groups behind its prophets, asking for intercession until it reaches Muhammad; this is the station at which God raises him.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري عن ابن عمر قال: إن الناس يصيرون يوم القيامة جثا كل أمة تتبع نبيها

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the sequence of prophets directing people to one another until Jesus directs them to Muhammad, who accepts the intercession.
rows.anchor:
وفي صحيح مسلم عن أنس قال حدثنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
" إذا كان يوم القيامة ماج الناس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet explicitly identifies the praised station as intercession; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor:
وروى الترمذي عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله:
" عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praised station is the great intercession for the assembly, which the prophets pass along until Muhammad intercedes to hasten judgment and relieve the people; it is particular to him.
rows.anchor: فيشفع هذه الشفاعة لأهل الموقف ليعجل حسابهم ويراحوا من هول

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash counts three Prophetic intercessions: general intercession, precedence in entering Paradise, and intercession for major sinners.
rows.anchor:
ولا فخر "
قال النقاش لرسول الله صلى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya counts two: the general intercession and intercession to remove sinners from Hell; prophets and scholars may share the latter.
rows.anchor: وشفاعة في إخراج المذنبين من النار.

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو الفضل عياض
rows.claim: Qadi ʿIyad counts five: general intercession, admission without reckoning, rescue of sinful monotheists from entering Hell, removal of sinners already in Hell, and raising Paradise residents' ranks.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة خمس شفاعات: العامة. والثانية في إدخال قوم الجنة

rows.speaker: الخوارج والمعتزلة
rows.claim: Kharijites and Muʿtazilites deny intercession for monotheists deserving Hell because of their rationalist doctrine of deserved punishment; they accept rank-raising intercession and the first assembly intercession.
rows.anchor: وهذه الشفاعة هي التي أنكرتها المبتدعة الخوارج

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qadi ʿIyad says early Muslims' requests for the Prophet's intercession are widely transmitted; asking is not blameworthy since it can ease reckoning or raise ranks, and rejecting it would also undermine supplication for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وعرف بالنقل المستفيض سؤال السلف الصالح لشفاعة النبي

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet's instruction after the call to prayer to ask God for the means and excellence and to raise him to the promised praised station; the supplicant earns his intercession.
rows.anchor: من قال حين يسمع النداء اللهم رب هذه الدعوة التامة والصلاة القائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view identifies the station with the banner of praise given to the Prophet; Qurtubi says it is compatible with intercession, and cites the report that all prophets are beneath his banner.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني أن المقام المحمود إعطاؤه لواء الحمد يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A group including Mujahid says God seats Muhammad with Him on a kursi; al-Tabari allows the report with far-fetched argument, while Qurtubi calls it remote absent a subtle interpretation and does not deny transmitting it.
rows.anchor: القول الثالث ما حكاه الطبري عن

rows.speaker: أبو داود السجستاني
rows.claim: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani is quoted as regarding one who denies the report as suspect because scholars have continually discussed it, provided its possibility is interpreted.
rows.anchor: وذكر النقاش عن أبي داود السجستاني أنه قال: من أنكر هذا الحديث

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar says two of Mujahid's interpretations were rejected by scholars: the seating report and reading the vision of God as merely awaiting reward.
rows.anchor: أبو عمر: ومجاهد وإن كان أحد الأئمة يتأول القرآن فإن له قولين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid is also reported to interpret the station as Muhammad being seated on the Throne.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أيضا في هذه الآية قال: يجلسه على العرش.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi explains that God's enthronement is without transfer, movement, or bodily state; seating Muhammad there would honor him without making him divine or removing his servanthood.
rows.anchor: ليس بمعنى الانتقال والزوال وتحويل الأحوال من القيام والقعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With Him” denotes rank, honor, favor, and high degree, not location, as in the expressions about those near their Lord, a house with God, and God being with the virtuous.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك عائد إلى الرتبة والمنزلة والحظوة والدرجة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation says the praised station is the Prophet's intercession to bring out of Hell those who will be released; Muslim reports it from Jabir.
rows.anchor: الرابع: إخراجه من النار بشفاعته من يخرج قاله جابر بن عبد الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ on why night worship leads to the praised station: God may make chosen acts causes of His grace, or the night offers private communion; the Prophet's degree is greatest, with unique gifts and intercession.
rows.anchor: اختلف العلماء في كون القيام بالليل سببا للمقام المحمود على قولين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God says “perhaps,” it is certain; maqāman is an accusative of place, meaning in or toward a station where one undertakes weighty matters.
rows.anchor: من الله عز وجل واجبة.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet defines the praised station as the place where he intercedes for his community.
rows.anchor:
قال:
" المقام المحمود هو المقام الذي أشفع فيه لأمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading asks for an honorable death and resurrection, linked to the promised praised station in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وابعثني يوم القيامة مبعث صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations ask to be brought into what is commanded and kept away from what is forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أدخلني في المأمور وأخرجني من المنهي.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits that the prayer asks for a safe departure from Mecca to Medina; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the prayer as the Prophet's departure from Mecca and safe entry into Mecca at the conquest.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو خروجه من مكة ودخوله مكة يوم الفتح آمنا.

rows.speaker: أبو سهل
rows.claim: Abu Sahl relates it to the Prophet's return from Tabuk amid hypocrites' threat that the more honored would expel the humiliated, asking for honorable entry and victory in Mecca.
rows.anchor: أبو سهل: حين رجع من تبوك وقد قال المنافقون:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the prayer asks for a truthful entry into the honor of prophethood and a truthful departure from it at death.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أدخلني في الأمر الذي أكرمتني به من النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading with damma makes madkhal and makhraj verbal nouns meaning admission and expulsion; Hasan, Abu al-Aliya, and Nasr ibn Asim read them with fatḥa as entry and exit.
rows.anchor: والمدخل والمخرج بضم الميم بمعنى الإدخال والإخراج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also interprets the prayer as asking for an honorable entry into the grave at death and exit at resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أدخلني القبر مدخل صدق عند الموت وأخرجني مخرج صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplication can apply generally to every affair, journey, work, and changing circumstance in life or death: asking God to make each departure and return sound.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الآية عامة في كل ما يتناول من الأمور ويحاول من الأسفار

rows.speaker: الشعبي وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and ʿIkrima explain “supporting authority” as a firm proof.
rows.anchor: الشعبي وعكرمة: أي حجة ثابتة.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains it as strength, victory, and making the religion prevail; God promised to take the Persian and Roman kingdoms and give them to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وذهب الحسن إلى أنه العز والنصر وإظهار دينه على الدين كله.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet struck the 360 idols around the Kaʿba with a stick, reciting this verse and saying falsehood neither begins nor restores anything; Bukhari and Tirmidhi grade the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: مكة عام الفتح وحول الكعبة ثلثمائة وستون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols numbered 360 because their worshippers honored one idol on a day and the greatest idols on two days.
rows.anchor: إنما كانت بهذا العدد لأنهم كانوا يعظمون في يوم صنما

rows.speaker: أبو عمر والقاضي عياض
rows.claim: The idols were fixed with lead and fell face-up or face-down whenever the Prophet prodded them; al-Qushayri says all fell face-first and were then broken.
rows.anchor:
وكان يقول:
" جاء الحق وزهق الباطل إن الباطل كان زهوقا "
حكاه أبو عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports breaking the polytheists' idols once they are overcome and, by extension, destroying tools whose only use is disobedience or prohibited diversion from God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على كسر نصب المشركين وجميع الأوثان إذ غلب

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir includes images made from clay or wood and objects with no utility beyond prohibited amusement; sale is barred except precious-metal idols altered into ingots or pieces.
rows.anchor: وفي معنى الأصنام الصور المتخذة من المدر والخشب

rows.speaker: المهلب
rows.claim: Al-Muhallab says owners may keep broken instruments if the fragments remain useful, unless the ruler sees burning them as a stricter financial punishment.
rows.anchor: وما كسر من آلات الباطل وكان في حبسها بعد كسرها منفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's principle also appears in the Prophet's report that Jesus will break the cross, kill swine, abolish jizya, and leave camels unused; it also supports destroying image-bearing curtains and instruments of amusement.
rows.anchor: والله لينزلن عيسى ابن مريم حكما عادلا فليكسرن الصليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Image making is forbidden: those who make images will be told to bring their creations to life, and authorities must prevent and change them.
rows.anchor: إن أصحاب هذه الصور يعذبون يوم القيامة ويقال لهم: أحيوا ما خلقتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The truth came” can mean Islam, the Qurʾān (Mujahid), or jihad; “falsehood departed” can mean idolatry or Satan (Mujahid). Qurtubi favors the broad sense: the law came with all that it contains.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد. والصواب تعميم اللفظ بالغاية الممكنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falsehood's departure means it is null and has no permanence, while truth endures; the same root describes a soul's passing away.
rows.anchor: إن الباطل كان زهوقا } أي لا بقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment through property has precedent: the Prophet removed ownership of a camel after its owner cursed it, Umar poured out milk diluted with water, and the Prophet considered burning homes of those absent from congregational prayer.
rows.anchor: فأزال ملكها عنها تأديبا لصاحبتها، وعقوبة لها فيما دعت عليه بما دعت به.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The majority read the verb with the first-person plural nūn; Mujahid has a light yāʾ reading, also transmitted from Hafs by al-Marwazi.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور بالنون. وقرأ مجاهد «وينزل» بالياء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Min can mark the Qurʾān as the source or clarify that what is sent down is Qurʾān; although some reject a partitive reading lest it imply part is not healing, Ibn Atiyya says the revelation is partial while all Qurʾān is healing.
rows.anchor: ويصح أن تكون لبيان الجنس كأنه قال: وننزل ما فيه شفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that whoever does not seek healing through the Qurʾān will not be healed.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر. «من لم يستشف بالقرآن فلا شفاه الله».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the Qurʾān healing for hearts by removing ignorance and doubt and uncovering what blocks understanding of God's signs and proofs.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه شفاء للقلوب بزوال الجهل عنها وإزالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes it as healing physical illness through recitation, seeking refuge, and similar remedies.
rows.anchor: الثاني شفاء من الأمراض الظاهرة بالرقى والتعوذ ونحوه.

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that he recited al-Fatiha seven times over a scorpion-stung tribal leader; the man recovered, and the Prophet approved the ruqya and eating its agreed sheep payment.
rows.anchor: فقرأت عليه «الحمد لله رب العالمين» سبع مرات فبرأ.

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Qurtubi introduces Abu Umama’s Prophetic report of Qurʾānic writing and a three-day healing regimen; its chain is given here and the prescribed text and method continue in the next segment.
rows.anchor: من حديث السري بن يحيى قال: حدثني المعتمر بن سليمان عن ليث بن أبي سليم عن الحسن عن أبي أمامة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says that during the Prophet's final illness he recited the protective sūrahs over himself; when gravely ill she recited them and wiped him with his blessed hand.
rows.anchor: وروى البخاري عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ينفث على نفسه في المرض الذي مات فيه بالمعوذات

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains nafth as blowing without saliva and tafl as blowing with saliva, supported by poetic usage.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري: قال اللغويون تفسير «نفث» نفخ نفخا ليس معه ريق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report prescribes a saffron or ochre Qurʾānic writing for several illnesses: wash it, drink three handfuls, perform ablution, pour it over the head, chest, and back, and pray for three days.
rows.anchor: ينفع باذن الله تعالى من البرص والجنون والجذام والبطن والسل والحمى والنفس أن تكتب بزعفران أو بمشق

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud is reported to dislike ruqya except with the protective sūrahs; al-Tabari says its transmitters include an unknown person, so it cannot establish law, and if sound it is mistaken or abrogated by the Prophet's approval of al-Fatiha ruqya.
rows.anchor: الثالثة: روى ابن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكره الرقى إلا بالمعوذات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since ruqya with two Qurʾānic sūrahs is permitted, ruqya with the rest of the Qurʾān is likewise permitted.
rows.anchor: وإذا جاز الرقي بالمعوذتين وهما سورتان من القرآن كانت الرقية بسائر القرآن مثلهما في الجواز إذ كله قرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the community's healing lies in a Qurʾānic verse, a lick of honey, or cupping; Rajaʾ al-Ghanawi says there is no healing for one who will not seek it through Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه عليه السلام أنه قال:

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab permits nushra, writing God's names or Qurʾān, washing the writing, and treating the patient; he allows undoing a spell affecting a spouse because useful remedies are not forbidden.
rows.anchor: فأجازها سعيد بن المسيب. قيل له: الرجل يؤخذ عن امرأته أيحل عنه وينشر؟

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid did not approve writing Qurʾānic verses, washing them, and making a frightened person drink the water; Aisha, however, recited the protective sūrahs into a vessel for the ill.
rows.anchor: ولم ير مجاهد أن تكتب آيات من القرآن ثم تغسل ثم يسقاه صاحب الفزع.

rows.speaker: الحسن وإبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi prohibit nushra; al-Nakhaʿi fears washing off Qurʾān may bring affliction, and al-Hasan transmits that Anas heard the Prophet call it satanic.
rows.anchor: ومنعها الحسن وإبراهيم النخعي، قال النخعى

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Dawud transmits Jabir's report that the Prophet called nushra an act of Satan.
rows.anchor: وقد روى أبو داود من حديث جابر ابن عبد الله قال

rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr calls the reports weak and interprets the prohibition as applying to practices outside revelation and recognized medicine; nushra can be a medicinal wash like the Prophet's ablution water.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر: وهذه آثار لينة ولها وجوه محتملة، وقد قيل

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An anonymous verse uses anfath to witness blowing without saliva.
rows.anchor: فإن يبرأ فلم أنفث عليه

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma uses yatfilu in a verse to witness blowing with saliva.
rows.anchor:
وقال ذو الرمة:
ومن جوف ماء عرمض الحول فوقه
متى يحس منه مائح القوم يتفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The censure targets preemptive pagan charms thought to ward off harm: only God averts affliction and grants health, so the Prophet forbade such pre-Islamic practices.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله تحذير مما كان أهل الجاهلية يصنعونه من تعليق التمائم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says an amulet hung after affliction has arrived is not the forbidden kind.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة قالت: ما تعلق بعد نزول البلاء فليس من التمائم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars dislike all amulets before and after illness, but Qurtubi regards the permissive distinction as stronger in transmitted evidence and reason.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أصح في الأثر والنظر إن شاء الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud's objection may concern non-Qurʾānic charms from diviners; seeking healing through the Qurʾān, hung or otherwise, is not shirk.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يريد بما كره تعليقه غير القرآن أشياء مأخوذة عن العرافين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the explicit marfuʿ report allowing ruqya without shirk and helping one's fellow should be relied upon, alongside the transmitted ruling for nushra from God's Book.
rows.anchor: قلت: قد ذكرنا النص في النشرة مرفوعا وأن ذلك لا يكون إلا من كتاب الله فليعتمد عليه.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik permits hanging writings containing God's names around the ill for blessing after illness begins, but not preemptively to ward off the evil eye; this is the view of a group of scholars.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: لا بأس بتعليق الكتب التي فيها أسماء الله عز وجل على أعناق المرضى

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: The Prophet taught a refuge prayer for someone frightened in sleep; Abdullah ibn Amr taught it to his children and wrote and hung it for those too young to learn.
rows.anchor:
وقد روى عبد الله بن عمرو قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إذا فزع أحدكم في نومه فليقل أعوذ بكلمات الله التامة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Opponents cite the report that whoever hangs an object is entrusted to it and Ibn Masʿud's forceful removal of an amulet, declaring his household free of shirk; he calls amulets, ruqya, and love charms shirk.
rows.anchor: ورأى ابن مسعود على أم ولده تميمة مربوطة فجبذها جبذا شديدا فقطعها وقال: إن آل ابن مسعود لأغنياء عن الشرك

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
rows.claim: ʿUqba ibn Amir reports the Prophet's curse on those who hang an amulet or shell charm.
rows.anchor: وروى عن عقبة بن عامر الجهنى قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد وأبو عمر
rows.claim: Al-Khalil defines tamima as a beaded necklace and wadiʿa as a shell; Abu Umar says scholars mean charms hung out of fear of the evil eye or other harm.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل بن أحمد: التميمة قلادة فيها عوذ، والودعة خرز. وقال أبو عمر: التميمة في كلام العرب القلادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān's mercy for believers relieves distress, cleanses faults, expiates sins, and brings reward for recitation.
rows.anchor: تفريج الكروب وتطهير العيوب وتكفير الذنوب مع ما تفضل به

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The Prophet says each Qurʾānic letter earns one good deed multiplied tenfold, not each disconnected letter-name as a whole; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih gharib.
rows.anchor: من قرأ حرفا من كتاب الله فله به حسنة والحسنة بعشر أمثالها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says everyone who sits with Qurʾān leaves with an increase or decrease, citing the verse about healing and loss.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: ما جالس أحد القرآن إلا قام عنه بزيادة أو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān increases the wrongdoers' loss because they reject it; similarly, it is guidance and healing for believers but a burden and blindness for unbelievers in 41:44.
rows.anchor: يزيد الظلمين إلا خسارا } لتكذيبهم. قال قتادة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the Qurʾān heals through its clear explanations of obligations and rulings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شفاء في الفرائض والأحكام لما فيه من البيان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For one who hangs Qurʾān, the promise “whoever hangs something is entrusted to it” means God will care for the person, since God is the one asked and trusted for Qurʾānic healing.
rows.anchor: فمن علق القرآن ينبغي أن يتولاه الله ولا يكله إلى غيره. لأنه تعالى هو المرغوب إليه والمتوكل عليه

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyab permits a Qurʾānic written charm if it is enclosed in a tube or protected sheet.
rows.anchor: وسئل ابن المسيب عن التعويذ أيعلق؟ قال: إذا كان في قصبة أو رقعة يحرز فلا بأس به.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak saw no harm in hanging a written portion of God's Book on a man even during intercourse or at the toilet.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك أنه لم يكن يرى بأسا أن يعلق الرجل الشيء من كتاب الله إذا وضعه عند الجماع وعند الغائط.

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي وابن سيرين
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Ali permits charms for children, and Ibn Sirin saw no harm in hanging a portion of Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: ورخص أبو جعفر محمد بن علي في التعويذ يعلق على الصبيان. وكان ابن سيرين لا يرى بأسا بالشيء من القرآن يعلقه الإنسان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people whom Qurʾān increases in loss turn from reflecting on God's signs and are ungrateful for His blessings; one report says the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: أي هؤلاء الذين يزيدهم القرآن خسارا صفتهم الإعراض عن تدبر آيات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To turn one's side away means arrogance and distance from fulfilling God's rights; the root denotes being far away, with related forms for making distant or moving apart.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «نأى بجانبه» أي تكبر وتباعد.

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's line uses al-muntaʾā for a far-off place, illustrating the root's sense of distance.
rows.anchor:
النابغة:
فإنك كالليل الذي هو

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, in Ibn Dhakwan's transmission, reads nāʾa with the hamza delayed, a metathesis of naʾā like raʾā and rāʾa; other readings are nuiʾa and the majority naʾā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر في رواية ابن ذكوان «ناء» مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further derivation connects the form to nawʾ, rising or standing, though the word may also mean falling or sitting as an antonym.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من النوء وهو النهوض والقيام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When poverty, illness, or hardship touches such a person, he despairs because he does not trust God's grace.
rows.anchor: أي إذا ناله شدة من فقر أو سقم أو بؤس يئس وقنط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak explain shākila as a person's side or direction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ناحيته. وقاله الضحاك. مجاهد: طبيعته.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also interprets it as a person's nature or temperament.
rows.anchor: وقاله الضحاك. مجاهد: طبيعته. وعنه: حدته. ابن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says shākila means one's religion.
rows.anchor: وعنه: حدته. ابن زيد: على دينه. الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret shākila as intention.
rows.anchor: على دينه. الحسن وقتادة: نيته. مقاتل: جبلته.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says it means one's innate constitution.
rows.anchor: وقتادة: نيته. مقاتل: جبلته. الفراء: على طريقته

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains shākila as the way and doctrine a person was formed to follow; another view makes it what seems most fitting and correct to one's belief.
rows.anchor: الفراء: على طريقته ومذهبه الذى جبل عليه.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A cited couplet says a person's deed resembles him and what he does is what he is suited for; shākila is also related to form, likeness, and appearance.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
كل امرئ يشبهه فعله
ما يفعل المرء فهو أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These explanations converge: people act in ways matching their origins and habitual character, which condemns unbelievers and praises believers.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأقوال كلها متقاربة والمعنى: أن كل أحد يعمل على ما يشاكل أصله

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi says this verse and the preceding verse were revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: نزلتا فى الوليد بن المغيرة ذكره المهدوى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows best who is truly guided, believer or unbeliever, and what each will ultimately become; another gloss takes “better guided” as quicker to accept or better in religion.
rows.anchor: بالمؤمن والكافر وما سيحصل من كل واحد منهم.

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr calls this the most hopeful verse because the servant is suited to sin while the Lord is suited to forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فإنه لا يشاكل بالعبد إلا العصيان ولا يشاكل بالرب إلا الغفران.

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar calls 40:2–3 the most hopeful passage because forgiveness of sins precedes acceptance of repentance.
rows.anchor: قدم غفران الذنوب على قبول

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: Uthman says 15:49 is the most hopeful verse: God tells His servants that He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
rows.anchor: فلم أر آية أحسن وأرجى من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says 39:53 is the most hopeful verse because God forgives all sins and forbids despair of His mercy.
rows.anchor: قل يعبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says 6:82 is the most hopeful verse, promising security and guidance to those whose faith is not mixed with wrongdoing.
rows.anchor:
فلم أر آية أحسن وأرجى من قوله تعالى:
الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit while he rested in a field; he paused without answering until revelation came with the response.
rows.anchor: في حرث وهو متكىء على عسيب إذ مر اليهود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the spirit asked about was Gabriel, and Ibn Abbas used to conceal this interpretation.
rows.anchor: هو جبريل قاله قتادة. قال: وكان ابن عباس يكتمه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other identifications say the spirit was Jesus or the Qurʾān; the latter is discussed in al-Shura.
rows.anchor: على ما يأتي بيانه في آخر الشورى.

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ali describes the spirit as an angel with 70,000 faces, each with 70,000 tongues and languages, praising God and generating an angel with every glorification.
rows.anchor: هو ملك من الملائكة له سبعون ألف وجه...

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya doubts that the elaborate angel report is authentic from Ali, though Qurtubi cites a chain for it through Ibn Abbas and another attribution to Ali.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وما أظن القول يصح عن علي رضي الله عنه.

rows.speaker: عطاء وابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ataa via Ibn Abbas instead describes an angel with eleven thousand wings and a thousand faces, praising God until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: الروح ملك له أحد عشر ألف جناح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the spirit as a host of God's creatures with hands and feet who eat food; Abu Salih similarly calls them creatures like humans but not humans.
rows.anchor: وعنه: جند من جنود الله لهم أيد وأرجل يأكلون الطعام

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says the spirit is a created species resembling human beings but not human beings.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح: الروح خلق كخلق بني آدم وليسوا ببني

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
rows.claim: Most exegetes say the question concerns the spirit that gives the body life; rationalists understand it as asking how spirit moves through and joins the body, an unknown matter.
rows.anchor: وذهب أكثر أهل التأويل إلى أنهم سألوه عن الروح الذي يكون به حياة الجسد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers leaving the identity unspecified: calling spirit God's command marks its greatness while withholding detail, showing people cannot know the essence of even their own selves and are still less able to comprehend their Creator.
rows.anchor: والصحيح الإبهام لقوله: «قل الروح من أمر ربي» دليل على خلق الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes disagree whether “you were given little knowledge” addresses only the questioners, Jews collectively, or all humankind; Qurtubi prefers all people and the majority reading “you were given.”
rows.anchor: اختلف فيمن خوطب بذلك فقالت فرقة: السائلون فقط.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Masʿud says “they were given” little knowledge, referring to Jews as a whole; it is also transmitted from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا هي قراءة ابن مسعود «وما أوتوا» ورواها عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews objected that they possessed the Torah and wisdom, but the Prophet answered by comparison with God's knowledge and defeated them; when asked whether Jews or his community were meant, he said “No,” meaning everyone.
rows.anchor: كيف لم نؤت من العلم إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's point about limited human knowledge is linked to the image of all trees on earth becoming pens in 31:27.
rows.anchor:
وفي هذا المعنى نزلت:
ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Quraysh asked about the spirit after Jews suggested asking about the sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and spirit; the first two stories were answered while the spirit was referred to God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن السائلين عن الروح هم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited by al-Mahdawi and other exegetes, says that the spirit is of God's command, known only to God.
rows.anchor: ذكره المهدوي وغيره من المفسرين عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could make the revealed Qurʾān disappear and cause people to forget it, just as He was able to reveal it; this connects to the previous statement that human knowledge is little.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن. أي كما قدرنا على إنزاله نقدر على إذهابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No protector could restore the Qurʾān against God; its continued presence is by God's mercy, either as a disconnected exception or because mercy prevents its removal.
rows.anchor: ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا } أي ناصرا يرده عليك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's great favor to Muhammad includes making him leader of Adam's descendants, granting the praised station, and giving him the noble Book.
rows.anchor: وأعطاك المقام المحمود وهذا الكتاب العزيز.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says trustworthiness will be the first religious quality lost and prayer the last; the Qurʾān will soon be removed from people's hearts and written copies, leaving them like beasts.
rows.anchor: أول ما تفقدون من دينكم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud repeats that the Qurʾān will be removed in a single night from hearts and manuscripts despite being memorized and taught; the account through Abu al-Ahwas and Shaddad ibn Maʿqil has a sound chain.
rows.anchor: كتاب الله يوشك أن يغضب الله لكتابه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says before the Hour the Qurʾān will return to where it descended with a bee-like hum, saying it came from God and returns to Him, yet was recited without being practiced; Qurtubi notes related marfuʿ reports from Ibn Amr and Hudhayfa.
rows.anchor: الثوب حتى لا يدرى ما صيام ولا

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa's report says Islam will wear away like embroidered cloth and scripture will be removed overnight; elders will retain the shahada without knowing prayer, fasting, sacrifice, or alms, yet that testimony saves them from Hell.
rows.anchor: يدرس الإسلام كما يدرس وشي الثوب حتى لا يدرى ما صيام ولا صلاة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: A report cited by al-Thaʿlabi and al-Ghaznawi says the Prophet warned that God might remove every page and heart containing books besides God's Book; a believer in whom God wills good will retain “there is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: ما هذه الكتب التي تكتبون أكتاب غير كتاب الله يوشك أن يغضب الله لكتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Supporters” means helpers or collaborators, like poets cooperating to complete a line; the verse responds to unbelievers who claimed they could produce something similar, affirming the Qurʾān's inimitability.
rows.anchor: أي عونا ونصيرا مثل ما يتعاون الشعراء على بيت شعر فيقيمونه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “they will not bring” answers the oath in the conditional, though it may also be jussive if the statement is treated as a condition.
rows.anchor: يأتون } جواب القسم في «لئن» وقد يجزم على إرادة الشرط.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A cited poetic line illustrates the conditional construction beginning with laʾin.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
لئن كان ما حدثته اليوم صادقا
أقم في نهار القيظ للشمس باديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has presented every kind of instructive example in the Qurʾān: signs, lessons, encouragement and warning, commands and prohibitions, earlier peoples' stories, Paradise, Hell, and Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي وجهنا القول فيه بكل مثل يجب به الاعتبار من الآيات والعبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people means Meccans: even after the truth was made clear and they were given respite, they persisted in denial.
rows.anchor: بين لهم الحق وفتح لهم وأمهلهم

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi rejects the Qadari argument that “refused except disbelief” means they had the power to choose faith at that moment; despite God's judgment and sealing their hearts, during respite they could seek truth and distinguish it from falsehood.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة للقدري في قولهم: لا يقال أبى إلا لمن أبى فعل
